```plato

    //==
    // # Isotropic elastic constants
    //
    // An isotropic material has exactly two independent elastic constants, and
    // `EngineeringMaterial` states them as Young's modulus and Poisson's ratio
    // because that is the pair a datasheet quotes. Analysis wants a different
    // pair. These are the standard conversions
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elastic_modulus); each is exact, so which
    // pair a caller holds is a matter of convenience only.
    //
    // Every one of them divides by a factor that vanishes at a limiting Poisson
    // ratio: the shear modulus at -1, the first parameter and the bulk modulus
    // at 0.5 (an incompressible material, which a displacement formulation
    // cannot represent). Real metals, plastics and ceramics sit well inside
    // those limits; a caller supplying 0.5 is asking for a division by zero.

    // The modulus of rigidity, mu: the ratio of shear stress to engineering
    // shear strain, and Lame's second parameter.
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shear_modulus)
    ShearModulus(m: EngineeringMaterial): Pressure
        => Pressure(m.YoungsModulus.Pascals / (2.0 * (1.0 + m.PoissonRatio)));
```
